stories.headline: AI startups raise across stages, from Exa's $250M round to seed deals for agent builders

key_facts.fact: Exa, which builds a search engine for AI agents, raised a $250M Series C led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $2.2B valuation, more than tripling its $700M valuation from a Series B eight months earlier; its API powers search for Cursor, Cognition, HubSpot and 400,000+ developers.

Viktor, an AI 'coworker' startup founded by former Meta engineers in Warsaw and Munich, raised a $75M Series A led by Accel after reaching $15M in annualized recurring revenue in roughly ten weeks and 12,000+ teams installed across Slack and Microsoft Teams.
Commure, which sells AI, revenue-cycle management and workflow-automation tools for healthcare providers, raised $70M led by General Catalyst at a $7B post-money valuation.
Paris-based Pivot, which develops AI tools for procurement and financial workflows, raised a $40M Series B co-led by Forestay Capital and Notion Capital.
NanoCo, maker of the open-source AI-agent platform NanoClaw (nearly 29,000 GitHub stars), raised a $12M seed led by Valley Capital Partners and said it turned down a $20M buyout offer.
Tribal AI raised a $10M seed led by Team8 to bring 'metadata-native' AI agents to enterprise systems including Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP, NetSuite and Workday.

stories.headline: AMD pledges over $10B in Taiwan to scale advanced packaging for next-gen AI chips

key_facts.fact: AMD announced more than $10 billion in investments across the Taiwan ecosystem to expand partnerships and scale advanced packaging manufacturing for AI infrastructure
AMD is working with Taiwan-based ASE and SPIL to develop next-generation wafer-based 2.5D bridge interconnect (EFB) technology to support its 6th Gen EPYC 'Venice' CPUs
AMD said it qualified the industry's first 2.5D panel-based EFB interconnect with packaging partner PTI
AMD's Helios rack-scale platform, using 'Venice' CPUs and Instinct MI450X GPUs, is on track for multi-gigawatt deployments beginning in the second half of 2026

stories.headline: AMD prices Ryzen AI Halo desktop at $3,999 and unveils Ryzen AI Max 400 chips to undercut Nvidia

key_facts.fact: AMD said its Mac Mini-sized Ryzen AI Halo PC will start at $3,999 with Ryzen AI Max 300 CPUs, with pre-orders beginning in June
AMD positions the Halo as a local-compute alternative to monthly cloud AI fees and a direct competitor to Nvidia's DGX Spark AI PC, which now costs $4,699
The Halo carries a 50 TOPS NPU, a Radeon GPU with 40 compute units and 128GB of unified memory, and can run Windows or Linux
AMD unveiled new Ryzen AI Max 400 chips led by the 16-core AI Max+ Pro 495 (5.2GHz boost, 55 TOPS NPU, up to 192GB unified memory), available in Q3 2026

stories.headline: Anthropic projects $10.9B Q2 revenue and its first-ever operating profit

key_facts.fact: Anthropic told investors it is on track to generate about $10.9 billion in revenue in the second (June) quarter, more than double the $4.8 billion it booked in the first quarter.
Hitting that target would mark Anthropic's first profitable quarter, with roughly $559 million in operating income, a 130% quarter-over-quarter revenue jump.
The single-quarter figure would exceed Anthropic's revenue for all of the prior year and implies an annualized run rate of roughly $44 billion.
The figures were disclosed to investors as part of an ongoing funding round and were first reported by The Wall Street Journal; Anthropic declined to comment.
The disclosure surfaced the same day as reports that OpenAI is preparing to file for an IPO, sharpening the rivalry narrative between the two leading AI labs.

stories.headline: Fed minutes show majority open to a rate hike as Iran-war inflation bites, ahead of Warsh's arrival

key_facts.fact: Minutes of the Fed's April 28-29 meeting, released May 20, showed a majority of policymakers felt 'some policy firming would likely become appropriate' if inflation continues to run persistently above the 2% target.
The FOMC left its policy rate unchanged in a range of 3.50%-3.75%, but four policymakers dissented - the most since 1992.
The Fed's preferred PCE inflation gauge was estimated at 3.5% in March, up from 2.8% in February, as the Iran war disrupted Middle East energy supplies.
The conflict has sent oil prices up by more than 50%; incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh inherits an increasingly hawkish committee.
Markets now see the Fed's next move as a possible hike rather than a cut; before the war they had priced in two 2026 rate cuts.

stories.headline: US gas prices near record over Memorial Day as Hormuz closure threatens $200 oil

key_facts.fact: The US national average gas price is expected to reach about $4.48 a gallon over Memorial Day weekend - 42% above last Memorial Day and the second-highest on record, according to GasBuddy.
Analysts warn the national average could hit $5 a gallon next month if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed; only 21% of Americans approve of Trump's handling of gas prices.
US commercial and emergency oil inventories plunged by the most on record last week, and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve has declined 10% since the war started, to a two-year low.

Wood Mackenzie warned a prolonged Strait of Hormuz closure is the single greatest threat to global energy markets in decades, with Brent potentially approaching $200/bbl in a worst case; more than 11 million b/d of Gulf crude and around 20% of global LNG supply are curtailed.
Oil prices spiked back above $100 per barrel as of May 20, remaining extremely volatile on conflicting signals about a US-Iran deal.

stories.headline: Intuit to cut 17% of staff, around 3,000 jobs, to refocus on AI

key_facts.fact: Intuit said on May 20 it would cut about 17% of its full-time workforce - roughly 3,000 of about 18,200 employees - to simplify its organizational structure and become 'a faster, leaner, more focused company'.
CEO Sasan Goodarzi's memo said the cuts will help the QuickBooks and TurboTax maker focus on bets like baking AI into its products.
Intuit expects $300 million to $340 million in restructuring charges, largely cash severance and benefits, recognized mostly in its fourth fiscal quarter ending July 31, 2026.
Intuit also trimmed its annual TurboTax revenue forecast; its shares fell about 14% after the bell amid lingering fears of AI disruption.
Intuit shares are down more than 40% so far this year amid worries that generative AI could disrupt its tax business, even as the S&P 500 has gained roughly 8%.

stories.headline: Iran reviews new US peace proposal as Trump says talks 'on the borderline'; CENTCOM boards Iranian tanker

key_facts.fact: Iran said on May 20 it was examining a new US proposal to end the Middle East war, conveyed via mediators, as Trump described negotiations as on the 'borderline' between a deal and renewed strikes and in their 'final stages'.
Trump said he was ready to proceed with further attacks on Iran if it did not agree to a deal, but suggested he could wait a few days to 'get the right answers'.

Trump and Netanyahu held a tense phone call; Netanyahu was highly skeptical of a Qatar/Pakistan-drafted 'letter of intent' that would officially end the war and open 30 days of negotiations on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and limiting Iran's nuclear program.
US Central Command said Marines boarded an Iranian-flagged oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman on May 20 on suspicion it was trying to violate the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority announced a new oversight zone in the Strait of Hormuz requiring transiting vessels to coordinate with Iranian authorities; Tehran said the US had failed to reopen the strait despite 'tricks'.
A ceasefire reached on April 8 through Pakistani mediation halted open fighting, but has not reopened the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil and LNG normally passes.

stories.headline: Microsoft open-sources RAMPART and Clarity, AI agent red-teaming and safety tools

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's AI Red Team open-sourced two tools: RAMPART, an agent test framework that encodes adversarial and benign scenarios as repeatable tests that run in CI, and Clarity, a structured 'sounding board' that helps teams decide whether they are building the right thing before writing code.

RAMPART is built on top of PyRIT, Microsoft's open red-teaming automation framework, and is aimed at engineers building systems, letting them turn red-team findings and AI incidents into lasting regression coverage.

Microsoft framed the release as making AI safety a continuous engineering discipline rather than a periodic checkpoint, motivated by the growing access and permissions that agents need to data like email, records and code repositories.

The company cited three reasons for investing in the tools: scaling red-teaming practices industry-wide, making incidents reproducible and verifying mitigations, and helping engineers think through the 'why' before the 'how' of building software.

stories.headline: Huang says Nvidia has 'largely conceded' China's AI chip market to Huawei, tells investors to 'expect nothing'

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company has 'largely conceded' China's AI chip market to Huawei as US export restrictions reshape the AI semiconductor landscape
Huang praised Huawei's strength, saying Nvidia has 'evacuated' the Chinese market
Huang said Nvidia told investors to 'expect nothing' regarding approvals to sell advanced chips into China
China once accounted for at least one-fifth of Nvidia's data center revenue but the company has been effectively shut out since the Trump administration required an export license in April
The comments came alongside Nvidia's blockbuster Q1 earnings report

stories.headline: Nvidia posts record $81.6B Q1 revenue, up 85%, adds $80B buyback as AI demand stays 'parabolic'

key_facts.fact: Nvidia reported record revenue of $81.6 billion for the quarter ended April 26, 2026, up 85% year-over-year and up 20% sequentially
Record Data Center revenue was $75.2 billion, up 92% year-over-year; Data Center networking revenue was a record $14.8 billion, up 199% year-over-year
GAAP net income rose 211% year-over-year to $58.3 billion, with diluted EPS of $2.39, up 214%
Nvidia's board approved an additional $80.0 billion share repurchase authorization and raised the quarterly dividend from $0.01 to $0.25 per share
Nvidia guided to $91.0 billion in Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue and said it is 'not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China' in that outlook
CEO Jensen Huang framed the quarter around AI infrastructure expansion

stories.headline: OpenAI preparing to confidentially file for IPO as soon as this week

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is preparing to confidentially file a draft of its IPO prospectus as soon as Friday, working with banks including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, in what could be one of the largest public-market debuts in history.
OpenAI is valued at more than $850 billion by private investors and is aiming to go public as early as September.
The Wall Street Journal was first to report the plan; an OpenAI representative said the company 'regularly evaluate[s] a range of strategic options' and that its 'focus remains on execution.'
The move comes two days after OpenAI fended off Elon Musk's court challenge; an IPOX analyst said resolving that legal overhang removed a major obstacle and let OpenAI accelerate its timeline.
OpenAI's filing would land the same week as SpaceX's IPO prospectus, forcing portfolio managers to weigh both AI-heavy listings side by side.

stories.headline: OpenAI reasoning model disproves Erdős's 80-year-old unit distance conjecture

key_facts.fact: An internal OpenAI general-purpose reasoning model disproved the planar unit distance conjecture, first posed by Paul Erdős in 1946, producing an infinite family of point sets that beats the long-assumed 'square grid' optimum with a polynomial improvement (n^(1+δ) for a fixed δ>0, versus the previously believed n^(1+o(1))).

The proof came from a new general-purpose reasoning model, not a system trained specifically for mathematics or theorem proving and not scaffolded for this problem; it surfaced while OpenAI was evaluating the model on a collection of Erdős problems.

The OpenAI team credited Lijie Chen with producing the proof using the internal model, and Mark Sellke and Mehtaab Sawhney with verifying correctness; a separate arXiv paper later made the exponent explicit, showing sets of n points with more than n^1.014 unit-distance pairs.

External mathematicians (Alon, Bloom, Gowers, Litt, Sawin, Shankar, Tsimerman, Wang and Matchett Wood) wrote a companion 'Remarks' paper presenting a human-digested version of the argument, which relies on tools from algebraic number theory; the AI proof was generated 'in one shot' and then refined through human interaction with Codex.

Fields medalist Tim Gowers called the result a milestone in AI mathematics, and observers framed it as the first time a prominent open math problem was solved autonomously by AI; mathematician Gil Kalai compared its potential significance to the 1976 computer-assisted proof of the four-color theorem.

stories.headline: Pentagon launches Cyber Command-NSA task force to deploy frontier AI in cyber ops

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon is standing up a task force spanning U.S. Cyber Command and the NSA to study how it can safely deploy leading AI models across its missions, including on 'high-side' systems holding the intelligence community's most sensitive secrets.
The lead role was assigned to a commander at Cyber Command, which a former senior national security official said signals CYBERCOM is 'more in charge, with NSA in support.'
Officials argued AI tools are becoming essential for detecting threats, prioritizing vulnerabilities and conducting both defensive and offensive cyber operations faster than adversaries.
The task force is not directly connected to the forthcoming White House AI executive order, though both CYBERCOM and NSA are expected to play a central role in new cybersecurity efforts.

The effort could increase pressure to lift the Defense Department's March 'supply chain risk' designation on Anthropic, whose Mythos model the company has said it is open to letting the government use in offensive cyber operations.

stories.headline: Xi and Putin hail ties at 'historic high' in Beijing, extend friendship treaty days after Trump visit

key_facts.fact: Xi Jinping hosted Vladimir Putin in Beijing on May 20, with Xi declaring China-Russia relations at a 'historic high' and a 'new stage', just days after Xi hosted US President Trump in China.
The two leaders oversaw the signing of more than 40 cooperation agreements spanning trade, technology, energy and media, and agreed to extend the 2001 Sino-Russian Treaty of Friendship.

Bilateral trade reached nearly $240 billion in 2025, with China Russia's largest trading partner for 16 years running; nearly all Russia-China import-export transactions are now settled in rubles and yuan.

The leaders signed a joint declaration on a 'multipolar world' and reached an understanding on the long-delayed Power of Siberia 2 gas pipeline, which would carry 50 billion cubic metres of Russian gas annually to China via Mongolia, though details remain under negotiation.
The Russia-China joint statement took aim at Trump's $175 billion 'Golden Dome' missile-defense plan and criticized the expiry of the last US-Russia arms control treaty.

stories.headline: Chinese humanoid maker Robot Era raises ~$140M A+ round led by Geely Capital

key_facts.fact: Embodied-AI robotics company Robot Era (Xingdong Jiyuan) completed an A+ round of about 1 billion yuan (roughly $140 million), led by Geely Capital
Co-investors include BAIC Industrial Investment, the Beijing AI Industry Investment Fund and the Beijing Robotics Industry Development Investment Fund
Founded about two years ago, Robot Era counts Alibaba, Haier Capital, Lenovo, Geely and BAIC among backers and is the only embodied-AI company in which Tsinghua University holds equity

The company's 2025 commercialization orders exceeded 500 million yuan, with deep partnerships with Geely, Renault, SF Express, TCL, Haier and Lenovo; its largest single logistics order was nearly 50 million yuan
Robot Era self-develops more than 95% of its components and products span the L7 full-size bipedal robot and its end-to-end VLA embodied model ERA-42

stories.headline: Samsung reaches last-minute wage deal, averting 18-day memory-chip strike amid global shortage

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics management and its largest labor union reached a last-minute wage deal on May 20, a day before a planned strike at the world's largest memory chipmaker
The agreement includes a 6.2% wage increase plus a new 'special semiconductor performance-based bonus' tied to AI chip earnings, set at 10.5% of business performance earnings without a cap
The planned 18-day strike (May 21–June 7) by nearly 48,000 union members is suspended, with the tentative deal put to a member vote from Friday through May 27
Industry estimates suggested an 18-day strike could have cut global DRAM supply by 3–4% and NAND flash by 2–3%, deepening an ongoing memory shortage
Samsung accounts for roughly one-third of the global DRAM market, and chips make up about 35% of South Korea's exports

stories.headline: SpaceX files publicly for what would be the largest IPO ever, revealing $4.9B 2025 loss

key_facts.fact: SpaceX publicly disclosed its IPO filing on May 20, set to be the largest IPO in history; it plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker 'SPCX', with a debut expected in late June.

SpaceX reported a net loss of $4.9 billion on $18.67 billion in revenue for 2025, swinging from a $791 million profit on $14.0 billion in revenue in 2024, as it invested heavily in xAI's AI infrastructure.
In Q1 2026 SpaceX booked a $4.3 billion net loss on $4.69 billion in revenue, and disclosed a debt load of $29.1 billion through the first quarter.
Starlink had about 10.3 million subscribers across 164 countries with more than 9,600 satellites by Q1 2026, and accounted for nearly 70% of SpaceX's revenue last year.
Elon Musk holds 85.1% of combined voting power through a dual-class stock structure; the offering targets a valuation of roughly $1.75 trillion and a raise of up to $75 billion.
The filing disclosed a $1.25 billion monthly compute contract with Anthropic; the AI segment (xAI plus X) posted a $6.36 billion operating loss on $3.20 billion in revenue in 2025.

stories.headline: SpaceX S-1 reveals Anthropic pays xAI $1.25B/month for compute; xAI to buy $2.8B more turbines

key_facts.fact: SpaceX's IPO filing revealed Anthropic will pay xAI $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 for compute, after Anthropic secured the entire output of the 300-megawatt Colossus 1 data center near Memphis
Either side can terminate the contract with 90 days' notice; SpaceX said the deal lets it 'monetize unused compute capacity'
Anthropic said it is expanding the partnership and will scale up GB200 capacity in xAI's Colossus 2 data center throughout June
The filing disclosed xAI will buy another $2.8 billion of turbines over three years, including a $2 billion deal for 'mobile gas turbines' — the type the NAACP is suing it over
xAI has been granted permits for 15 turbines at its Memphis site but was operating 46 as of a few weeks ago

stories.headline: Stability AI releases Stable Audio 3.0 with six-minute songs and open weights

key_facts.fact: Stability AI released Stable Audio 3.0, a family of four models (three with open weights, one API-only) trained entirely on licensed data, capable of generating music tracks more than six minutes long.

The medium and large models were trained on a mix of licensed audio from AudioSparx (806,284 audios) plus Creative Commons recordings from Freesound, with copyrighted material filtered out using a music tagger.

Three variants (3.0 Small, 3.0 Small SFX and 3.0 Medium) are downloadable on Hugging Face while 3.0 Large is API-only; the company says 3.0 Small is the only model capable of full music composition on-device.
With fully licensed training data and legal indemnification for enterprise customers, Stability is positioning itself against rivals Suno and Udio, which face music-industry copyright lawsuits.
Users own the audio they generate and can commercialize it under the Stability AI Community License; organizations with more than $1M in annual revenue need an Enterprise License.
